## Micron and SK Hynix Commit Billions to Memory Capacity, but Supply Is Largely Deferred to 2028

Supply deferred to 2028 means memory pricing and HBM allocation remain structurally tight for the next several quarters, supporting MU's pricing power thesis and validating long exposure to memory-adjacent AI infrastructure names.

- Both MU and SK Hynix are committing large-scale capex to memory capacity expansion.
- The headline signals the bulk of new supply will not arrive before 2028, creating a multi-year gap between spend and availability.
- The timing gap supports sustained memory pricing tightness and reinforces HBM allocation dynamics through at least 2027.
- No specific dollar figures per company or facility details are disclosed beyond the aggregate 'billions' characterization.
